statement.source_mapping: /spec/source.txt is formalized in /workspace/Research/Submission.lean: exactProductTree maps leaves to exact real products; roundedProductTree maps leaves to Model.mul; roundedDotProduct applies roundedSum to the rounded products. The target quantifies over every supplied Model and every Tree (ℝ × ℝ), assumes only ((tree.depth + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * model.u < 1, and asserts existence of a Tree ℝ related to exactProductTree tree by IsPerturbation (gamma (tree.depth + 1) model.u), whose exactSum equals roundedDotProduct model tree. All five supplied support modules are copied byte-for-byte unchanged. Statement revision record: initial statement, no prior statement revised; /spec/feedback.json was absent. lake build succeeded; the final theorem proof alone has a temporary sorry for the next proof role.

verification.limitation: Compilation alone does not establish the original theorem or algorithm. Semantic review is required.

report.target_evidence: The translated final target itself asserts the complete universally quantified backward-error theorem relative to exactProductTree(T), including the gamma(depth(T)+1,M.u) bound and equality with roundedDotProduct(M,T). Its constructions explicitly define one rounded multiplication per input leaf and rounded addition at every internal node. Existential perturbation witnesses satisfy the source construction policy.

requirements.requirement: Prove the full universally quantified dot-product backward-error theorem.
requirements.evidence: The sole target directly quantifies over every model M and every tree T of real pairs and concludes existence of P with both IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u), exactProductTree(T), P) and exactSum(P) = roundedDotProduct(M,T). This is the full final conclusion, with no further composition required.

requirements.requirement: Relate perturbations to exact componentwise products x_i*y_i.
requirements.evidence: exactProductTree maps each original leaf (a,b) to exact ab and preserves all ordered nodes. The target uses this very tree as the reference for the same-shaped perturbation tree P, requiring |y_i-a_i*b_i| <= gamma(d+1,u)*|a_i*b_i| at every corresponding leaf.

requirements.requirement: Account for one rounded multiplication per leaf.
requirements.evidence: roundedProductTree maps each leaf (a,b) to r(ab), and roundedDotProduct applies roundedSum to this tree. The final target includes one multiplication error in its d+1 bound; roundedSum does not round again at a leaf.

requirements.requirement: Account for every rounded tree addition in the reduction.
requirements.evidence: roundedSum(M,node(L,R)) = r(roundedSum(M,L)+roundedSum(M,R)). Every internal node of the original tree is preserved. The final equality therefore includes every rounded addition along the specified reduction.

requirements.requirement: Establish the gamma(depth+1,u) componentwise perturbation bound.
requirements.evidence: The target directly asserts the uniform componentwise bound gamma(d+1,u) = (d+1)*u/(1-(d+1)*u). IsPerturbation requires this bound at every leaf and recursively on both subtrees. With depth(leaf)=0, d+1 counts one product rounding and at most d additions, including the single-leaf case.

requirements.requirement: Use only the stated model and smallness assumptions without assuming or restricting the conclusion.
requirements.evidence: The target assumes only (d+1)*u < 1 beyond relative-error model membership: u >= 0 and for every real z some delta satisfies |delta| <= u and r(z)=z*(1+delta). It has no exact-arithmetic, balance, sign, nonzero-input, or fixed-size restriction and does not assume the perturbation conclusion.

limitations: This review evaluates the supplied mathematical translation and its stated final target and constructions; it does not inspect Lean code or independently certify proof checking.
